scope: Room Beacon and Private Relay evaluated against the same local-first fixture and six human-psychology gates.
limitation: Each entry is a structured design hypothesis. It records no participant, observation, rate, success claim, or approval.

conditions.frame: Ordinary social setting with no impairment framing and moderate distraction.
Ordinary cognition with competing conversation and high acoustic distraction.
Alcohol-framed cognitive-load condition with ordinary social noise; not a diagnosis or individual prediction.
Alcohol-framed cognitive-load condition with competing conversation and high acoustic distraction; not a drinking instruction.

cells.risk: The group can mistake an attributed prompt for a verified public statement.
cells.safeConstraint: Keep the persistent game beacon before commit and use neutral, explicit truth labels only after reveal.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay reduces public staging but needs the same truth boundary.

cells.risk: The blind holder can act before the group finishes its judgment.
cells.safeConstraint: Expose one idempotent holder tap and confirm the committed state without revealing the card.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay has direct reading but still needs an idempotent commit.

cells.risk: The first confident voice can become the room answer.
cells.safeConstraint: Use a short neutral prompt that allows another view before the holder commits; do not reward shouting or speed.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay shifts pressure to the private player rather than removing it.

cells.risk: Attribution, quote, and role instruction compete for attention.
cells.safeConstraint: Use one shared statement, concise role copy, and a stable game-context marker.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay may reduce distance demand but needs equally concise private instruction.

cells.risk: Assistive technology can reveal the card to the blind holder.
cells.safeConstraint: Hide active-card descendants from the holder while preserving an equivalent tap-only round.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay permits active-player reading but must protect handoff.

cells.risk: A misfire can feel like a group member caused an unfair outcome.
cells.safeConstraint: Describe recovery neutrally, retain the round where safe, and never silently reinterpret a commit.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay needs the same neutral repair language plus shutter recovery.

cells.risk: Noise makes the quote or group reaction more salient than the game marker.
cells.safeConstraint: Keep the game beacon visible, textual, and non-color-dependent throughout the active round.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay also needs a visible game marker because private attention can be divided.

cells.risk: A holder may commit on an incomplete or misheard cue.
cells.safeConstraint: Make the tap target large, single-purpose, untimed, and inert after the first commit.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay avoids blind cues but requires the same duplicate guard.

cells.risk: Quieter disagreement can disappear under competing speech.
cells.safeConstraint: Do not add timers or escalating motion; leave an explicit pause-safe moment before commit.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay can support a quieter private judgment but changes the social ritual.

cells.risk: Players may retain the quote but lose role or next-action meaning.
cells.safeConstraint: Prioritize role instruction and controls over decorative information; preserve an untimed fallback.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay removes distance reading, not noisy attention.

cells.risk: A hurried role transition can expose the active card.
cells.safeConstraint: Keep holder privacy fail-closed and make the screen-facing role explicit before the round.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay requires a blocking shutter between players.

cells.risk: Recovery instructions can be missed and lead to repeated inputs.
cells.safeConstraint: Offer one visible, calm recovery action and preserve no-more-than-one score change.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay must discard interrupted private state instead of risking disclosure.

cells.risk: Salient attribution or timer cues can eclipse the product's truth posture.
cells.safeConstraint: Use plain text stating that this is a game prompt and the reveal determines status.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay needs the identical truth wording.

cells.risk: Fast movement or a prepotent response can create an accidental commit.
cells.safeConstraint: Keep the motion-independent tap path primary-capable and reducer commits idempotent.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay reduces motion ambiguity but not premature taps.

cells.risk: Social confidence can be treated as authority.
cells.safeConstraint: Avoid punitive countdowns and preserve a neutral chance to reconsider before one group commit.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay protects a private answer but can isolate the player.

cells.risk: Players may forget which person can see content or which control is live.
cells.safeConstraint: Make role, current control, and next action visible at the decision point.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay still needs a clear active-player and handoff boundary.

cells.risk: Quick transitions increase protected-card leakage risk.
cells.safeConstraint: Never reveal the active card to the holder through visual or assistive-technology paths.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay must conceal score and content during handoff.

cells.risk: An accidental answer can cause blame or pressure to undo history.
cells.safeConstraint: Show a neutral result path, prevent duplicate scores, and give a safe next round.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay uses the same commit integrity with a privacy-first restart.

cells.risk: The loudest cue can make the game look like an authenticity claim.
cells.safeConstraint: Maintain a high-contrast text beacon and never present source confidence before reveal.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay shares the required pre-reveal neutrality.

cells.risk: Noise and rushed movement compound duplicate-commit risk.
cells.safeConstraint: Make the first tap final, ignore repeats, and provide a clearly labeled non-motion path.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay needs the same reducer-level duplicate defense.

cells.risk: A loud early answer can end discussion before another person contributes.
cells.safeConstraint: Keep play untimed and avoid feedback that celebrates the fastest speaker.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay offers a different pressure pattern, not proof of lower pressure.

cells.risk: Long content and recovery instructions can exceed available attention.
cells.safeConstraint: Use bounded fixture length, progressive truth review, and concise recovery copy.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay supports closer reading but must retain the same content-state clarity.

cells.risk: A chaotic pass can reveal card or result to the wrong person.
cells.safeConstraint: Use explicit role states and fail closed if a protected transition is interrupted.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay's shutter is the required recovery countermodel.

cells.risk: Repeated misfires can create a punitive group dynamic.
cells.safeConstraint: Use calm language, bounded retries, and a new round rather than an unsafe undo.
cells.countermodelComparison: Private Relay discards interrupted private material before repair.

cells.risk: Private reading can make the prompt appear like a verified claim.
cells.safeConstraint: Keep the same persistent game context and neutral post-commit truth reveal.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon makes shared context more visible but has distance constraints.

cells.risk: A player can tap twice while moving through a private turn.
cells.safeConstraint: Accept one idempotent answer and make result transition unambiguous.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon also needs blind-holder duplicate protection.

cells.risk: Private answering can suppress the group's alternative interpretation.
cells.safeConstraint: Describe it as an equal accessibility/recovery mode, not as the social default or a consensus cure.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon preserves discussion but has public-pressure risk.

cells.risk: The player can lose track of handoff or review state.
cells.safeConstraint: Use a full-screen shutter and a single next action between private turns.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon needs shared role recall instead of handoff recall.

cells.risk: Prior content or score can remain visible to the next player.
cells.safeConstraint: Conceal score and card during handoff; discard interrupted private state.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon protects the blind holder during the active card.

cells.risk: A player can feel blamed if a handoff exposes a result.
cells.safeConstraint: Use a neutral shutter recovery that starts a fresh protected turn.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon can retain shared context when interruption is safe.

cells.risk: A player can miss the game marker while reacting to the group.
cells.safeConstraint: Keep the game marker persistent and textual rather than relying on spoken guidance.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon has the same marker requirement at group scale.

cells.risk: Competing conversation can prompt a premature tap.
cells.safeConstraint: Use large labeled taps, no timer, and immutable first-commit behavior.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon needs the same one-commit reducer behavior.

cells.risk: The group may pressure the private player without seeing the card.
cells.safeConstraint: Do not imply that private play eliminates social pressure; preserve clear player ownership.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon makes group input overt and should not privilege it.

cells.risk: Handoff instructions can be lost in competing audio.
cells.safeConstraint: Use a visual shutter with one explicit ready action and no audio dependency.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon prioritizes shared visual hierarchy instead.

cells.risk: A hurried pass can bypass a privacy transition.
cells.safeConstraint: Block the next card until the new player explicitly continues from the shutter.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon must block holder access to active-card semantics.

cells.risk: An interruption can surface a previous private result.
cells.safeConstraint: Discard the private turn on backgrounding and state the recovery plainly.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon can pause only because the card remains role-protected.

cells.risk: A salient attribution can outweigh the later truth state.
cells.safeConstraint: Retain neutral pre-reveal language and state truth in words after commit.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon requires the same truth contract.

cells.risk: Quick taps can create accidental answers.
cells.safeConstraint: Make response state irreversible but non-punitive, with no duplicate score.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon adds blind-holder movement risk to this shared constraint.

cells.risk: The active player may defer to an external loud opinion.
cells.safeConstraint: Do not present speed, confidence, or alcohol framing as a success measure.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon needs a visible pause for multiple voices.

cells.risk: The player can lose the current role across handoff.
cells.safeConstraint: Keep one active-player label and a clear shutter boundary.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon needs one holder/screen-facing role label.

cells.risk: An interrupted pass can expose private content to another person.
cells.safeConstraint: Fail closed by discarding private state and concealing the score before handoff.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon's active-card privacy applies to the holder instead.

cells.risk: A discarded turn can feel punitive.
cells.safeConstraint: Explain that the protected prior turn was not shown and offer a fresh turn without blame.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon recovery preserves shared context when safe.

cells.risk: A private prompt can be screenshotted or misread as an external claim.
cells.safeConstraint: Keep the game context visible and withhold source-confidence cues before reveal.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon shares this capture-safety requirement.

cells.risk: Noise, rush, and movement can cause repeat taps.
cells.safeConstraint: Use an idempotent reducer, disabled repeats, and a no-motion primary path.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon must also ignore repeated answer actions.

cells.risk: Private play can be framed as opting out of the group.
cells.safeConstraint: Describe it as an equal route with the same score, review, report, and rematch semantics.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon remains primary ritual, not a superior-access path.

cells.risk: Long copy and handoff instructions may not be retained.
cells.safeConstraint: Use short copy, progressive review, large targets, and one visible next action.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon needs the same content budget at shared distance.

cells.risk: The phone can be passed before privacy is restored.
cells.safeConstraint: Use a blocking shutter, conceal the score, and discard state on interruption.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon instead hides active content from the holder and assistive technology.

cells.risk: A failed handoff can become a social accusation.
cells.safeConstraint: Use neutral recovery copy and start a fresh protected turn without revealing why.
cells.countermodelComparison: Room Beacon similarly avoids blaming the holder for a misfire.
